0.translation: ⟦shared:0⟧⟦shared:1⟧Combine original FASTA, GFF3 and standard BLAST tables into a traceable comparison. Inspect inputs, choose a display subset, then compare chord and full-length views.⟦shared:2⟧⟦shared:3⟧

2.translation: Starting with original files, compare observed similarity intervals and CDS across four source genomes. FASTA/GFF3 identifiers and sources match the [four-sequence case](⟦shared:0⟧). Standard BLAST tables retain original values; conversion and physical source rows are recorded in examples/blastn-standard/provenance.csv.

3.translation: Package code is MIT-licensed. Original database records and third-party catalogues retain their own source terms; package licensing does not automatically relicense every input. The manual archive carries unchanged files, SHA256 and provenance. The separate EMALE format examples retain gggenomes MIT source licensing in GGGENOMES-LICENSE.txt.

5.translation: Extract the [input bundle](⟦shared:0⟧) so your working directory contains ⟦shared:1⟧.

9.translation: FASTA supplies IDs and lengths, GFF3 supplies annotation ranges and strands, and BLAST supplies observed alignments. The empty validation summary means no issues were reported for these inputs.

13.translation: Keep alignments with at least 80% identity and an alignment length of at least 500 bp. For the chord view, show up to six of the longest CDS per sequence so the links remain readable.

20.translation:
Read sequence labels first, then source-strand feature arrows and interval links.
Ribbons encode existing aligned intervals and mapped identity; their crossing is
not itself evidence of a rearrangement. The selected features remain visibly
separate from the much wider alignment spans. Use the full input tables when
scientific interpretation needs annotations outside this display subset.

21.translation: ## Inspect all annotations in a linear view ⟦shared:0⟧

24.translation:
This view draws all imported annotations. Ribbons connect adjacent displayed
sequences by default; retaining every comparison is an explicit layer decision.
The bp scale bar belongs to collinear coordinates. See [local views](⟦shared:0⟧)
for cropping, source-coordinate axes and independent windows, and
[output](⟦shared:1⟧) to preview and save at the gallery's stated dimensions.

25.translation: ## Keep the evidence with the figure ⟦shared:0⟧

26.translation:
The input archive contains unmodified FASTA/GFF3/BLAST files, a SHA256 manifest
and the shared example script. The plot manifest records the code hash, PNG device,
width, height and dpi. The accession names identify source records; a drawing is
not a replacement for the original annotations or alignment evidence.

28.translation: Backbones use ⟦shared:0⟧ and ⟦shared:1⟧. Ribbons use IDs and endpoints on both sequences. This example also filters on ⟦shared:2⟧ and ⟦shared:1⟧. See [alignment inputs](⟦shared:3⟧).

30.translation: Check that IDs agree across the tables, inspect filtering reports and verify that guides encode identity and strand. Use the overview to locate regions, then focus a neighbourhood to study a CDS.

33.translation: Save the plot just created to the working directory; use matching dimensions for preview.

36.translation: Preview with view_ggchord at the declared width/height and save with ggsave at matching dimensions. Check IDs, source strands, endpoint directions, selection reports, legend units and hidden-label reasons. A successful PNG does not certify font portability across PDF/SVG viewers. Keep complete source tables, display subsets, parameters, version and input hashes. Download the [asset/provenance record](⟦shared:0⟧).
